topics.summary: A cancer treatment using drugs to kill fast-growing cells throughout the body.
topics.how_it_works: Chemotherapy drugs interfere with the cell cycle, specifically targeting cells that divide rapidly. By damaging the DNA or RNA, it prevents them from reproducing.

topics.summary: Treatment that boosts the body's natural defenses to fight cancer.
topics.how_it_works: It uses substances made by the body or in a lab to improve or restore immune system function. Checkpoint inhibitors, for instance, take the 'brakes' off the immune system so it can recognize and attack cancer cells.

topics.summary: High-energy particles or waves used to destroy cancer cells.
topics.how_it_works: High doses of radiation create small breaks in the DNA inside cancer cells, preventing them from growing and causing them to die.

topics.summary: Drugs designed to target specific molecules that help cancer grow.
topics.how_it_works: These drugs block the action of specific enzymes, proteins, or other molecules that signal cancer cells to grow and spread.

topics.summary: Treatment that slows or stops the growth of cancers that use hormones to grow.
topics.how_it_works: It acts by blocking the body's ability to produce hormones or by interfering with how hormones behave in the body.

topics.summary: Procedures that restore blood-forming stem cells in people who have had theirs destroyed by high doses of chemo or radiation.
topics.how_it_works: Healthy stem cells are infused into the bloodstream, where they travel to the bone marrow and begin producing new, healthy blood cells.

topics.summary: Cancer that forms in the cells of the breasts.
topics.how_it_works: Cells in the breast tissue begin to grow uncontrollably, often forming a tumor that can be seen on an x-ray or felt as a lump.
contact_care_team_if: swollen lymph nodes under the arm

topics.summary: Cancer that begins in the lungs and most often occurs in people who smoke.
topics.how_it_works: Malignant tumors develop in the tissues of the lung, usually in the cells lining air passages.

topics.summary: Cancer that starts in the colon or the rectum.
topics.how_it_works: Most start as growths called polyps on the inner lining of the colon or rectum. Over time, some polyps can turn into cancer.

topics.summary: Cancer in a man's prostate, a small walnut-sized gland that produces seminal fluid.
topics.how_it_works: Cancer cells develop in the prostate and can grow slowly or aggressively to invade nearby tissue.

topics.summary: Cancer of the body's blood-forming tissues, including the bone marrow and the lymphatic system.
topics.how_it_works: The bone marrow produces excessive amounts of abnormal white blood cells, which don't function properly and crowd out healthy cells.

topics.summary: Cancer of the lymphatic system, which is part of the body's germ-fighting network.
topics.how_it_works: Lymphocytes (white blood cells) grow out of control and collect in lymph nodes, making it harder for the body to fight infection.

topics.summary: Cancer that begins in the organ lying behind the lower part of the stomach.
topics.how_it_works: Malignant cells form in the tissues of the pancreas, often spreading rapidly to nearby organs.

topics.summary: The most serious type of skin cancer, developing in the cells that produce melanin.
topics.how_it_works: Occurs when pigment-producing cells become cancerous; often triggered by UV radiation damage.
contact_care_team_if: a mole that bleeds or itches

topics.summary: The spread of cancer from the primary site to other parts of the body.
topics.how_it_works: Cancer cells break away from the original tumor, travel through the blood or lymph, and form new tumors in other organs.

topics.summary: A decrease in or disappearance of signs and symptoms of cancer.
topics.how_it_works: Tests indicate that the cancer is responding to treatment or is no longer detectable.

topics.summary: An examination of tissue removed from a living body to discover the presence, cause, or extent of a disease.
topics.how_it_works: A sample of cells is extracted (via needle or surgery) and analyzed by a pathologist.

topics.summary: Cancer that begins in the skin or in tissues that line or cover internal organs.
topics.how_it_works: These cancers start in epithelial cells, which make up the skin and the linings of organs like the liver or kidneys.

topics.summary: A type of cancer that begins in bone or in the soft tissues of the body.
topics.how_it_works: Arises from mesenchymal cells, which form connective tissue, fat, muscle, blood vessels, and bone.
common_side_effects: lump that can be felt through skin

topics.summary: A growth that is not cancerous and does not spread to other parts of the body.
topics.how_it_works: Cells grow abnormally but do not invade nearby tissue or metastasize.
contact_care_team_if: sudden change in size of growth

topics.summary: Cells that can invade and destroy nearby tissue and spread to other parts of the body.
topics.how_it_works: Uncontrolled cell division that leads to the invasion of healthy tissue and systemic spread.
contact_care_team_if: any new or worsening cancer symptoms

topics.summary: Specialized medical care for people living with a serious illness.
topics.how_it_works: Focuses on providing relief from the symptoms and stress of the illness to improve quality of life for both the patient and the family.

topics.summary: The process of finding out how much cancer is in a person's body and where it’s located.
topics.how_it_works: Uses physical exams, imaging, and biopsies to determine the tumor size (T), lymph node involvement (N), and metastasis (M).

topics.summary: Treatment given after the primary treatment to lower the risk that the cancer will come back.
topics.how_it_works: Aims to kill any remaining microscopic cancer cells that could not be removed during surgery.

topics.summary: Treatment given as a first step to shrink a tumor before the main treatment.
topics.how_it_works: Usually chemo or radiation given before surgery to make the tumor easier to remove.

topics.summary: Research studies that test how well new medical approaches work in people.
topics.how_it_works: Patients volunteer to test new drugs or combinations under strict supervision to determine safety and efficacy.

topics.summary: A condition in which there is a lower-than-normal number of neutrophils (a type of white blood cell).
topics.how_it_works: Often a side effect of chemotherapy, making the patient highly susceptible to infection.

topics.summary: A doctor who has special training in diagnosing and treating cancer.
topics.how_it_works: Coordinates the patient's care plan, including medical, surgical, or radiation oncology.

topics.summary: An approach to patient care that allows doctors to select treatments based on a genetic understanding of their disease.
topics.how_it_works: Uses genetic testing of a tumor to find the specific mutations driving the cancer and matches them with targeted drugs.

topics.summary: A test done on a sample of blood to look for cancer cells or pieces of DNA from a tumor.
topics.how_it_works: Identifies circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) or circulating tumor cells (CTCs) shed into the blood.
